Your impact begins here

As Associate Consumer Pricing Director, you will lead pricing and deal strategy for non-traditional channels across EUCAN: e-health and online channels, online pharmacies and e-commerce, direct-to-employer and private health insurance. Obesity is your primary focus. You will shape how deals are designed, negotiated and put into practice, while protecting the pricing system that supports access across markets. Your work helps more people living with serious chronic disease reach treatment, through routes that fit real life.

What you’ll bring

You combine pricing expertise with commercial understanding and the confidence to influence decisions at every level.

• An M.Sc. or MBA in economics, business administration, finance or a similar field.

• At least 7 years of experience in pharma pricing, market access, business analytics or finance, from an affiliate, regional or headquarter role, or from a consultancy.

• Proven expertise in international reference pricing (IRP) and parallel trade risk, HTA, launch planning, mature brand and generic life-cycle management, and budget  and forecasting processes.

• Strong project and stakeholder management, and strong interpersonal skills.

• Strong negotiation skills, with the ability to communicate and influence across multiple levels, internally and externally.

• Business acumen and a problem-solving mindset that turns analysis into decisions that support patient access and business goals.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience negotiating commercial deals.

• Experience with e-commerce or digital health business models.

What you’ll do

You will be the recognised expert on commercial channel pricing in EUCAN, turning analysis into clear recommendations and deals that work in practice.

Lead commercial pricing and deal strategy for non-traditional channels

• Set the pricing strategy for e-health and online prescribers, online pharmacies and e-commerce, direct-to-employer and private health insurance across EUCAN, with obesity as the focus and the wider portfolio in view.

• Develop deal structures and pricing guardrails for non-traditional players, in alignment with IO Pricing.

• Lead gross-to-net and discount analytics to inform deal design and pricing decisions.

Lead the design, negotiation and governance of deals with key accounts

• Give recommendations and input to key account management for EUCAN-level providers, and support negotiations with selected key accounts.

• Support affiliates in implementing agreed deals, from negotiation preparation and deal terms to follow-up.

• Develop and present recommendations to the EUCAN Pricing Council and to IO and HQ pricing teams.

Safeguard the core pricing system across the portfolio

• Assess and mitigate IRP and parallel trade risks arising from net prices in commercial channels.

• Monitor the online channel, competitor prices and the market access, HTA and pricing landscape across EUCAN, and flag risks and opportunities to your manager and the Pricing Council.

• Contribute to launch planning for new products, indications and formulations, and lead pricing life-cycle strategies for mature brands and generic and biosimilar insights, in coordination with Commercial.

• Support key processes, including annual budget planning and long-term forecasting, with recommendations, analytics and quality assurance.

Build pricing analytics, insights and capabilities

• Lead the development of commercial pricing capabilities, tools and best practices across the region and affiliates, and mentor colleagues in your field of expertise.

• Keep affiliates informed with timely communication, and share relevant best practices and information.

• Contribute to cross-functional team processes, including team meetings, budget and launch planning, and manage the budget for your own tasks and external projects.

Who you’ll work with

You will join EUCAN Pricing & Market Access in International Operations, where colleagues work across markets to serve people around the world and help improve health at scale. Your responsibility covers the EUCAN region and your assigned therapy area(s), with specific countries managed as key accounts.

Your closest partners are the affiliates you support in negotiations and deal implementation, key account management, and Business Development. You will also work with IO and HQ pricing teams and present to the EUCAN Pricing Council, so decisions are made with clarity and at pace. You will report to Senior Director Pricing & Market Access

What you can expect here

You will work in an international environment where your expertise shapes decisions across Europe and Canada.

The role offers real breadth with opportunities to work on Obesity and collaborate across the value chain and build new skills through regional and affiliate work. You will be trusted to take ownership and make your voice heard, supported to perform at your best in a team that combines curiosity, collaboration and ambition.

Salary

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 931,670.00 to 1,369,660.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits

The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

As Advanced Process Supporter, you will keep a tablet packaging line in Måløv running steadily and in line with GMP. Operators turn to you when a process issue, quality question or deviation needs a clear answer, and you use what you learn to improve how the line works. Your work helps tablets packed in blisters reach people around the world on time and in the highest quality.

What you’ll bring

This is a hands-on role close to production, so we are looking for someone with manufacturing experience who is ready to take ownership.

• A Bachelor’s degree in engineering (e.g. production, manufacturing, pharmaceutical, chemical, or mechanical) or another relevant discipline.

• Extensive experience in process support, production support, process engineering or a similar manufacturing support role.

• Experience from a GMP-regulated or other regulated manufacturing environment, with sound judgement on quality and compliance in live production situations.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and enjoyment in working through complex production challenges.

• Fluency in Danish and English.

• A structured way of working, with consistent follow-up until issues are closed.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience from a packaging line.

• Basic familiarity with PAS-X.

• Experience with process improvement.

What you’ll do

• You will support the packaging line day to day, so production stays stable and compliant, and look for ways to make it better.

• Provide daily process support to the packaging line, including technical guidance, knowledge sharing and training within the production area.

• Troubleshoot and resolve process-, operator- and quality-related issues, such as procedures not followed correctly or product questions that arise during production.

• Make sure production follows GMP requirements and approved procedures.

• Handle and support deviations, change requests and other quality activities, using structured problem solving and root cause analysis.

• Identify and lead smaller improvement initiatives that strengthen process performance, quality and productivity.

• Participate in a planned 24-hour on-call rotation, typically 1–2 days per week, including out-of-hours support.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Process Support team in Tablets & Finished Products at the Måløv site, part of Global Manufacturing & Supply. The team of 11 supports the packaging line and includes seven process supporters, plus reviewers and an editor. Collaboration, development and continuous improvement are central to how it works.

Your closest partners are operators, technicians, QA, maintenance and production management. You will gather information from the floor, build strong working relationships and coordinate people so issues are solved quickly. When something stalls, you speak up and help move it forward.

What you can expect here

This role puts you at the centre of a production line that people depend on, and gives you the room to shape how it runs. You will learn from colleagues who know the line well and get training and onboarding with backup until you feel confident. We value people who raise the bar, so clear expectations, honest feedback and the chance to lead smaller improvements are part of the everyday work. Your results are noticed and recognised, and you keep building new skills through hands-on experience and relevant learning offerings.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200 - 838,100 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to keep production moving and improve how it works, apply for the Advanced Process Supporter role by 5 November 2026, with your CV in English. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so apply as soon as you can.

For further information about the position, please contact Trine Duelund at TDTR@novonordisk.com.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Schmidt Hammer Lassen is looking for an ambitious Business Development Manager to join our team in Copenhagen on a full-time basis.

As our new Business Development Manager, you will play a hands-on role in shaping new opportunities for our practice in collaboration with partners, teams, and clients across markets, disciplines, and cultures.

What you will do:

• Lead prequalification processes, coordinating materials and internal and external stakeholders to ensure timely, high-quality submissions.

• Support the formation of strong, well-aligned project teams for tenders and strategic opportunities in key markets.

• Research clients, market trends, and relevant background information to identify new opportunities and inform strategic decisions.

• Create engaging business-development and communications content, including award submissions, announcements, and trade-show materials.

• Maintain knowledge of trends and developments within the studio’s practices and markets.

• Strengthening the studios’ network and relationships with collaborators and potential clients.

• Helping expand SHL’s reach and visibility within the industry through outreach, events and industry networks.

We are looking for someone who has:

• A bachelor’s degree in architecture, communication, business or a related field

• 2+ years of relevant professional experience in the architectural sector.

• Experience supporting PQs and pitches for both public and private clients.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate ideas in a way that inspires confidence and engagement. Fluency in a Scandinavian language is an advantage, but not a requirement.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work independently while contributing positively to a collaborative team with multiple deadlines.

• Strong stakeholder management skills and experience coordinating both internally and externally.

• A strong visual eye and confidence creating clear, high-quality presentation and communication material in Adobe Creative Suite (primarily InDesign).

About Schmidt Hammer Lassen

Driven by a deep responsibility towards our planet, we strive for an architecture that transforms our understanding of the world by giving back to the environment, to communities, and to individuals. We design places of cultural resonance. We embed ourselves in each context to understand the intangible. Regardless of their place in the world, our projects live and breathe effortlessly in their context, making their inhabitants feel truly at home.

We continuously work to maintain a high-quality, well-managed architecture studio that delivers excellent results for our clients while providing strong support, clarity, and development opportunities for our organization.

For more information about our studio: www.shl.dk

Practical details

This is a full-time position based at our Copenhagen studio.

Qualified and interested candidates are encouraged to upload their application and CV through our online recruitment system. We review applications on an ongoing basis and will close the posting once the right candidate has been found.

We do not accept applications submitted outside our recruitment system, and all applications are handled in accordance with applicable data-protection regulations.

Salary will be negotiated based on qualifications.

Questions

Please contact Head of People & Culture, Majbritt Vendelbo, at mve@shl.dk.

We look forward to hearing from you!

As Quality Manager, you will bring a strong operational background from an SCM role and use that experience to strengthen quality, process discipline, and continuous improvement across procurement, warehousing and logistics. This role is ideal for someone who has developed from hands-on supply chain responsibilities towards quality management, operational excellence, and structured process improvement.

You will work closely with the Head of Procurement and Head of Warehouse to enhance operational performance, introduce lean efforts, supplier and stakeholder management. Together you will work closely to implement and improve practical workflows, controls, and supplier interfaces. You will identify gaps, remove inefficiencies, support Lean optimization, and ensure that agreed improvements are embedded, followed up, and translated into measurable performance gains.

The role will have a reporting line to our Chief HSEQ & SCM Officer and work closely with the IMS team to ensure alignment with the company’s Integrated Management System.

**Your Responsibilities

**

• 
Improvement of our end-to-end workflows across Procurement, Warehouse, and Logistics, including clear procedures, work instructions, controls, templates, handovers, and escalation paths.

• 
Strengthening supplier interfaces by defining and following up on requirements for ordering, confirmations, documentation, delivery performance, quality issues, and corrective actions.

• 
Lead daily Lean improvements through operational walk-throughs, waste and bottleneck analysis, root-cause analysis, and action plans with clear owners and deadlines; verify that implemented changes deliver the intended results.

• 
Work with the Head of Procurement and Head of Warehouse to set improvement priorities, maintain SCM KPIs, and action trackers, resolve recurring operational issues, Non-conformance, and improve performance against agreed targets.

• 
Perform recurring checks of process compliance, master data, transaction quality, and equipment inspection, calibration, and certification status; document deviations, coordinate corrections, and escalate overdue items.

• 
Implement and embed new ways of working by preparing practical training and user guidance, following up on adoption in daily operations, and coordinating process changes and IMS documentation with the IMS team.

**Qualifications

**

• 
A strong operational background from Supply Chain Management, with experience from procurement, warehousing, logistics, inventory control, asset management, or a comparable SCM function.

• 
Hands-on experience implementing and improving workflows, supplier interfaces, procedures, controls, and ways of working together with operational process owners.

• 
Practical experience applying Lean, Continuous Improvement, or similar methods to improve day-to-day operational performance.

• 
Structured and analytical approach to problem-solving.

• 
Strong communication and collaboration skills.

• 
Proficiency in English and Danish both written and spoken.

• 
Strong knowledge of the Microsoft Office suite.

**Preferred Qualifications

**

• 
Experience with ISO 9001.

• 
Experience with internal audits and compliance-related activities.

• 
Experience with ERP systems, preferably Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

• 
Experience with calibrations, certifications, and/or asset management.

• 
Experience from the wind industry or another technical service organization.

**Why Join Us?

**

• 
Become part of a growing international company within renewable energy.

• 
Take on a central role with significant influence on the development of our Supply Chain Management function.

• 
Work in a collaborative environment focused on knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.

• 
Contribute to the green transition through the global wind industry.

• 
Excellent opportunities for both personal and professional development.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

We are looking for a Product Compliance Manager to join Veo's newly established Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) team.

As Veo continues to grow, we navigate a broad range of regulatory requirements across our products and business, from certifications, product safety, and environmental regulation to market access and broader compliance obligations.

In this role, you will focus on product-related regulatory compliance and certifications, while also working across Veo's broader compliance agenda. You will work closely with colleagues across Hardware, Product Development, Production, Procurement and other parts of the business to understand applicable requirements and help translate them into practical processes and solutions.

You will join a small GRC team with a broad mandate and significant exposure across Veo. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys understanding regulation, technology, and business.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Coordinate Veo's product certification and market-access activities across relevant markets, working closely with Hardware, Production and other internal stakeholders.

• Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

• Develop and maintain a structured overview of regulatory and certification requirements applicable to Veo's products throughout their lifecycle.

• Drive and coordinate implementation of regulatory and compliance requirements across relevant business functions, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate documentation and timely follow-up.

• Work with regulatory frameworks relevant to Veo's products, including areas such as product safety, batteries, electrical and electronic equipment, environmental requirements, waste and recycling obligations and related product compliance requirements.

• Coordinate with external certification bodies, laboratories, consultants and other specialists where required.

• Maintain and develop compliance documentation, certification records, technical files, declarations and other evidence required to demonstrate compliance.

• Support the assessment of regulatory and compliance implications when Veo enters new markets, introduces new products or makes material changes to existing products.

• Support Veo's broader compliance activities, including policies, procedures, monitoring, due diligence, risk assessments and training.

• Support customer, auditor and other stakeholder requests relating to compliance and certifications.

• Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

**Your qualifications:

**

• Relevant higher education in engineering, technology, law, business, quality/compliance, or another relevant discipline.

• Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

• Experience working with regulatory requirements affecting hardware or electronic products is an advantage.

• Experience with one or more areas such as product safety, product certifications, battery regulation, electrical/electronic equipment regulation, environmental product requirements, waste/recycling regulation or similar regulatory regimes.

• Experience coordinating certification processes, testing, technical documentation, declarations or interactions with certification bodies and laboratories is highly relevant.

• Broader compliance experience, for example within sanctions and export controls, third-party due diligence, anti-bribery and corruption or other corporate compliance areas, is an advantage.

• An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

• A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

• Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

At Veo, the Governance, Risk & Compliance team provides oversight, coordination and assurance across the company. We work closely with teams throughout Veo to ensure that regulatory requirements and risks are identified, appropriately owned and effectively managed.

You will report to the Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance and will have considerable opportunity to shape how Veo approaches compliance as the company continues to grow.

Contact Martin Eger Larsen one mel@veo.co if you have any questions

We're looking for a marketing intern who wants to manage their own projects and develop creatives that get published.

Great camping experiences start long before guests arrive. At CompuSoft, we build the software that helps campsites turn that first booking into a memorable stay. We’re looking for a marketing intern who wants to take ownership of projects and create content that gets published.

Who We Are

We’re a Danish software company with roots in the camping industry and a story that began in 1987. Today, more than 600 campsites, holiday resorts, attractions, and other tourism businesses use our solutions.

Our technology brings together online booking, guest management, payments, guest apps, and self-service tools. We help businesses simplify daily operations, giving their teams more time to focus on their guests.

With development, sales, and support in-house, we work closely across teams and with our customers to keep improving our solutions.

Your Role:

Your work will cover content, communication, and digital marketing. We’ll shape the internship around your strengths and interests, so tell us what you enjoy working on.

You’ll have your own projects with clear goals and also support the team where needed.

Your tasks may include:

• Writing LinkedIn posts, newsletter articles, and customer stories.

• Creating photos, short videos, and simple graphics.

• Helping plan and run campaigns across our four markets, from trade fairs and webinars to customer events.

• Keeping our messaging clear and consistent across our website, emails, and sales materials.

• Working with our website, email flows, and HubSpot, and tracking results to understand what works.

• Testing new ideas, including ways to use AI tools in our daily marketing work.

...

Who we're looking for

You’re studying marketing, communication, journalism, digital media, or a related subject, and your programme includes an internship.

We hope you:

• Write well in Danish and English. Swedish, Norwegian, or German is a bonus.

• Are curious and enjoy figuring things out independently.

• Have some experience with content, social media, or digital marketing through your studies, work, or personal projects.

• Feel comfortable asking questions and sharing ideas.

You don’t need to know about campsites or software. We’ll teach you that.

What We Offer

You can expect:

• Real responsibility and work you can include in your portfolio.

• A dedicated contact person who makes time for you and provides honest feedback.

• Experience in a growing SaaS company with marketing activities across four markets.

• A place in a team that works closely with sales, product, and customer success.

• A relaxed workplace where we take the work seriously, but not ourselves.

How to Apply

Send a short application and your CV through the application form before December 10. Tell us who you are, what you’d like to work on, and show us one thing you’ve made: a post, an article, a video, or a campaign.

We review applications as they arrive and may fill the position before the deadline.

Help build a stronger and more consistent approach to maintenance at Site Gentofte. As CMMS & Spare Parts Management Lead, you will help centralise and strengthen our computerised maintenance management system (CMMS) and spare parts management, supporting implementation of the Novo Nordisk Reliability and Maintenance blueprint. By connecting systems, master data, processes and people, you will help make maintenance activities more reliable and create practical improvements for daily production.

What you’ll bring

You bring hands-on expertise in SAP Plant Maintenance (PM) and Materials Management (MM), combined with an understanding of how maintenance systems and reliable master data support production. Just as importantly, you can turn complex requirements into clear ways of working and bring stakeholders with you.

To succeed in this role, you have:

• Proven experience in setting up, configuring and implementing SAP PM and SAP MM.

• In-depth knowledge of SAP PM and SAP MM and how they support maintenance and spare parts processes.

• At least two years of experience with reliability and maintenance of production equipment in a regulated environment.

• Experience with spare parts management, maintenance master data, task lists and related processes.

• Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to collaborate across different functions.

• The ability to structure your own work, drive several initiatives in parallel and communicate fluently in English.

You are motivated by creating structure, improving processes and helping colleagues use systems and data to support reliable production.

What you’ll do

Your focus will be on creating robust and consistent processes that work in practice. You will:

• Drive implementation and continuous improvement of CMMS and spare parts management processes in line with the Novo Nordisk Reliability and Maintenance blueprint.

• Support CMMS super users and colleagues responsible for spare parts management in establishing consistent ways of working.

• Act as a subject matter expert and facilitator for CMMS and spare parts management.

• Manage and improve master data for spare parts, maintenance schedules and equipment, working with stakeholders to maintain the required inputs.

• Work with production departments to support a seamless flow of maintenance activities and data and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

• Understand operational needs across production and translate them into improvements that create value in day-to-day work.

Who you’ll work with

You will join cGMP & Operations Support within Production Support at Site Gentofte. Production Support is a technical department of approximately 100 employees responsible for critical utilities and technical support for projects and operations.

Your immediate team has 15 colleagues with diverse educational backgrounds. One part of the team supports operations within CMMS and spare parts management across Site Gentofte, while another provides GMP support for utilities and quality processes across Production Support.

As CMMS and spare parts management are being centralised in the team, you will work closely with colleagues across production, maintenance execution and other support functions. You will join an environment with experienced colleagues where knowledge sharing and collaboration are part of everyday work.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to help shape a newly established function, including its structure, processes and ways of collaborating. The role combines development of maintenance capabilities with a close connection to daily production, giving you exposure to a broad stakeholder landscape across Site Gentofte.

You will work at the intersection of systems, maintenance and production, using your expertise to establish solutions that support reliable maintenance processes, high-quality master data and effective spare parts management.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

As Process Engineer in API Manufacturing in Kalundborg, you will help bring a new product into large-scale production. You will combine your chemistry or biochemistry knowledge with process data to understand the molecule, the reactions and the purification steps, and turn that insight into stable, compliant and efficient manufacturing. As the product moves from project into operations, you will take growing ownership and help more people living with diabetes and other serious chronic diseases get the treatment they need.

What you’ll bring

You understand manufacturing at a molecular, chemical and biochemical level, take ownership and stay constructive when priorities change. You will typically have:

• A Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD in biochemistry, chemistry, biotechnology, biomedicine, chemical engineering or another relevant life-science discipline.

• Relevant experience from pharmaceutical manufacturing, API production, biotechnology or another chemistry-intensive production environment.

• Practical knowledge of one or more areas such as chemical modification, protein chemistry, organic chemistry, downstream processing, purification, filtration or HPLC.

• Working knowledge of cGMP in a regulated setting.

• Strong English communication skills and the ability to share knowledge, collaborate across functions and influence decisions.

• Curiosity, a proactive approach and enjoyment in solving complex challenges.

Useful, but not essential:

• Hands-on experience with deviations, investigations, change control, qualification or validation.

• Experience with data analysis to identify correlations and root causes in process data.

What you’ll do

You will strengthen product and process understanding in a state-of-the-art production environment and support the transfer of a new product from development into operations.

• Build a detailed understanding of how the molecule, chemical modification, protein chemistry and purification steps affect the final product.

• Analyse process data to find correlations and root causes, and turn the findings into practical improvements and monitoring.

• Support qualification and validation activities in line with cGMP requirements, and the implementation of new products and processes.

• Take ownership of product-related activities such as deviations, investigations, change requests, product transfers and continuous improvement.

• Share your specialist knowledge, contribute to technical decisions and help build capability in a growing team.

Priorities may shift as the organisation moves into operations. You will have the chance to help shape effective ways of working and how the team supports products and processes in the future.

Who you’ll work with

You will join a growing team in API Manufacturing at Novo Manufacturing Kalundborg, a leading production hub for insulins and GLP-1 analogues that support millions of people living with diabetes and other chronic diseases. Several colleagues are joining the area at the same time, so you can influence the team’s technical direction and its specialist culture from the start.

You will work with specialists in production, development, quality and engineering who continuously improve how we manufacture. Together you will connect scientific insight to practical decisions, with broad exposure to product changes, development activities and manufacturing challenges.

Please note: there will be manufacturing, storage or handling of semi-finished or finished GLP-1 products in the work location (building), regardless of whether you will directly handle the products.

What you can expect here

You will be supported to grow your skills while being trusted to take ownership and make your voice heard. Working across production, development, quality and engineering gives you broad experience of the value chain, and a growing team means room to build your expertise alongside colleagues who share it. FPRT is looking for a Senior Composite Process Technology Manager for our new composite production in Vojens, Denmark, and Moment Professionals manages the recruitment on our behalf. Your everyday at FPRT

You report to the Chief Production Officer, Composite Manufacturing, and you build and lead the composite technology team of composite process engineers and materials and polymer engineers. You work closely with Production, Quality and NDT, HSE, Maintenance and Engineering, Planning and Supply Chain, and you support the competency and qualification standards for supervisors, technicians and operators together with Production and HR. You are the technical authority for composite manufacturing processes, with the mandate to define process parameters, technical standards and work instructions, and to require technical containment, a process review or a production stop when process integrity, product quality or safety is at risk.

Production starts from an existing process that is being transferred to Vojens, and experienced specialists from the group come to the site to hand it over. You lead the technical transfer and convert it into FPRT-controlled specifications, work instructions, training content and qualification requirements, and you define the technical requirements for equipment, tooling, fixtures, utilities and production conditions through trials, pilot builds and ramp-up. You make sure FPRT has clear local ownership of the critical processes and keeps the technical knowledge for the long term. From day one, you are expected to spot where a step can be done smarter and to have the composite understanding to back that view.

Your time is split between the desk and the floor. You own process flows, critical parameters, material requirements and process-control standards, and you define process qualification, inspection points, acceptance criteria and quality gates together with Quality and NDT. When a process starts to drift, you are the primary escalation point: you go to the floor, lead root-cause analysis, non-conformity investigations and corrective actions, and turn the lessons into updated standards and training. The weight of the role lies in the moulding stage and the material side of the process: resin systems, reinforcements such as carbon fibre, adhesives, curing and the conditions that decide whether porosity and voids are designed out or created. You need a sound grasp of finishing, but your depth is in why a part comes out of the mould as it does.

This is a greenfield site. New buildings are under construction on the site, systems are being selected, and support functions such as maintenance, IT and HR are being built in parallel. In the first period you will help shape how things are done well beyond your own field, and the composite team grows as production scales towards stable serial production.

The role is based in Vojens, and being on site is essential during the build-up. English is the working language in instructions and with colleagues across the group. Danish is a strong advantage in daily life on the floor, and if you are not fluent yet, your willingness to learn it counts.

Real authority over the processes you own, greenfield impact with no legacy to work around, a professional, international environment with a clear mission and purpose, a modern office with gym, sauna and social spaces, and top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

To succeed in the role…

…you do not need to have carried a manager title or to come from defence. What matters is that you know composite technology in depth: why a resin system behaves as it does, what creates strength and what creates defects, and how the environment affects the part. You may come from composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence or another high-performance industry, and work today in process or manufacturing engineering, production, materials or as a technical composite specialist. You also take pride in:

• challenging an established method, including one handed over by experienced colleagues, and agreeing on a better answer together.

• taking ownership and making decisions where little is written down yet.

• going to the floor when a process drifts and staying until the root cause is found.

• turning know-how into standards, instructions and training that engineers and operators can work from.

• developing engineers through technical reviews, coaching and structured problem solving.

What you need to bring:

• Either a relevant technical degree or equivalent strong industrial experience, and at least five years in composite manufacturing, process engineering, manufacturing engineering or materials engineering.

• Practical experience with industrial manufacturing of fibre-reinforced composite components and thermoset resin systems such as epoxy, phenolic or other thermosets, and hands-on experience with one or more of resin infusion or transfer processes, filament winding, lay-up, moulding, curing, bonding or composite machining and finishing.

• A proven track record of developing, transferring, industrialising, qualifying or stabilising manufacturing processes into repeatable production, with a solid grip on process control, documentation, process risk assessment, root-cause analysis, non-conformity handling and technical change management.

• Experience leading, mentoring or coaching engineers and production specialists, or acting as their technical authority.

• Fluent English, written and spoken. Danish is a strong advantage, or the willingness to learn it.

It is an advantage if you:

• come from advanced composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence, pressure vessels, automotive or another high-performance application.

• have worked with large or structurally critical components, such as aerospace and defence structures, casings, filament-wound products, UAV components or wind turbine blades.

• have taken part in a greenfield factory, a new production line, a technology transfer or a major ramp-up.

• live within commuting distance of 6500 Vojens, Denmark.

jobs.description:
Join the Physics Group at the Department of Materials and Production at Aalborg University and contribute to research on the quantum properties of matter at the scale of individual atoms and molecules. This is a full-time, fixed-term PhD stipend for three years, commencing on 1 January 2027 or soon hereafter

**Your work tasks

**The Department of Materials and Production is looking for a PhD candidate in experimental physics to investigate how molecular complexes can be used to engineer quantum properties in materials. The project addresses fundamental questions in quantum science while contributing knowledge that may support future applications within electronics, sensing and energy harvesting. You will become part of the Physics Group and work in an international research collaboration funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark.

Your research will focus on preparing and investigating molecular complexes on crystalline surfaces. You will deposit molecular complexes by electrospray techniques under ultra-high-vacuum conditions and study their structural and electronic properties using low-temperature scanning tunnelling microscopy and scanning tunnelling spectroscopy. The work will involve planning and conducting experiments, documenting methods and results, analysing and discussing data, and communicating findings clearly within the research collaboration and through relevant scientific channels. You will carry out a substantial part of the research independently while collaborating closely with researchers in the project.

Your competencies You hold a master's degree in physics, nanoscience or a closely related field. You have a solid experimental background within physics, surface science or nanoscience, together with documented experience in scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy, ultra-high-vacuum techniques, cryogenic systems, surface science and electrospray deposition.

You can organise and conduct experimental research in a systematic manner, from the planning of measurements to the documentation, analysis and interpretation of results. You communicate methods and findings clearly in English, both in writing and in dialogue with other researchers. The position calls for a researcher who can take responsibility for their own work while contributing constructively to a collaborative and international research environment.

**Qualification requirements

**PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are

You will join the Physics Group at the Department of Materials and Production, where research activities explore materials and physical phenomena relevant to both fundamental science and future technologies. In this position, you will work at the intersection of molecular science, surface science and quantum materials research, with access to a research environment in which experimental methods and scientific discussion form the basis for developing new knowledge.

As part of an international collaboration, you will have the opportunity to engage with researchers across disciplines and contribute to a research project with both scientific depth and technological relevance. The position offers a strong foundation for further work in academic research, advanced experimental physics or research-intensive development environments.

**How to apply

**Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades)

• Other relevant documents

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.

Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

**Salary and terms of employment

**The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement).

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

QuNorth is looking for a Quantum Error Correction (QEC) Lead to help develop and lead our collaborative Quantum Error Correction program, in addition to participating in other aspects of operationalizing Magne, QuNorth’s Neutral Atom quantum computer, in a fast-paced but stable startup environment.

QuNorth is a new Nordic Hub for quantum exploration, providing the region’s enterprises, researchers, and startups with the capability to test, learn, and build on Magne, a world-leading Level 2 quantum computer. With strong backing from EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation, QuNorth will operate Magne as a shared platform for Nordic industries, research organisations, and start-ups. Our aim is to provide the access, tools, expertise, and support needed to explore new quantum applications across all relevant areas, including, but not limited to, life sciences, innovative materials, biochemistry, and AI.

Magne’s physical layer, developed by Atom Computing, includes 1200+ Ytterbium-171 atoms, serving as physical qubits with all-to-all connectivity. It can be operated seamlessly in logical mode enabled by Microsoft, providing tens of logical qubits depending on QEC code. Magne can also be operated in physical mode with mid-circuit measurement and feedforward, which in conjunction with its all-to-all connectivity at scale turns Magne into an excellent platform for exploration of novel QEC techniques, unconstrained by “chip topology”. We envision QEC projects and broader QEC-related partnerships to be a strong component of QuNorth’s portfolio. Working directly with the CTO, and interfacing with the CPO team and QuNorth’s users and partners, the QEC Lead will help shape this key component of the QuNorth portfolio. This role will, at least initially, be mostly a technical leadership role, rather than a managerial position.

We are a small and committed team working to build QuNorth from the ground up as a reliable and transparent organization that contributes to the long-term strength of the Nordic quantum computing ecosystem.

Your Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will eagerly engage in many of the following directions:

• Lead QuNorth’s technical work on quantum error correction, including strategy, architecture assessment, simulation, benchmarking, resource estimation, and roadmap development.

• Evaluate and compare QEC codes, decoding approaches, logical gate schemes, error models, and fault-tolerant architectures.

• Work with hardware, software, and theory collaborators to connect QEC requirements and assumptions to realistic device constraints.

• Help identify which QEC approaches are most relevant to QuNorth’s mission and which are not.

• Work closely with QuNorth’s CTO and Quantum Applications and Algorithms Lead to explore the interplay between applications, algorithms, QCVV, compilation, QEC, noise, error mitigation, and logical-mode operation, including opportunities for integration and co-design.

• Represent QuNorth in collaborations, including with universities, research institutes, startups, and enterprises.

• Contribute to proposals, grant applications, reports, publications, presentations, and internal documents.

• Help recruit, mentor, and coordinate future team members working on QEC, quantum architecture, simulation, and related topics.

• Participate in broader company-building work, including technical due diligence, collaborator or partner discussions, product strategy, documentation, and operational tasks.

• Use AI tools effectively and responsibly to accelerate research, coding, literature review, writing, planning, analysis, operations, and internal workflows.

• Help establish a high standard for scientific rigor, clear communication, and effective execution within the company.

Your Experience and Qualifications:

We expect strong candidates to have many of the following:

• A PhD or equivalent experience required in quantum information, quantum computing, physics, computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience in QEC beyond PhD.

• Deep understanding of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

• Deep familiarity with topics such as surface codes, qLDPC codes, color codes, bosonic codes, subsystem codes, concatenated codes, holographic codes, and other conventional or emerging QEC approaches.

• ‘Hands-on’ experience with decoding algorithms, error models, threshold analysis, logical error rates, resource estimation, and architecture-level tradeoffs.

• Deep familiarity with QCVV techniques, including benchmarking approaches.

• Deep familiarity with protocols for mitigation and characterization of noise and error, and their relationship with QEC and relevant thresholds.

• Strong programming experience, preferably in Python or similar scientific computing environments, with experience developing simulations, analysis workflows, notebooks, benchmarking tools, or research software.

• Experience collaborating across disciplines with comfort, especially between theory, software, and experimental teams.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfort working in an early-stage environment where priorities evolve and everyone contributes beyond their formal job title.

• Practical experience using AI tools such as LLMs, coding assistants, literature tools, agentic workflows, and AI-enabled analysis environments.

• Good judgment about when AI tools are useful, when they are unreliable, and how to verify their outputs.

The Team:

The position is based in our new offices at Rønnegade 6 in Copenhagen, where Magne is also currently being built. You will be part of the Technology team under the CTO, and will interact closely with the Product team under the CPO and the rest of QuNorth as well.

Like many start-ups, we are building QuNorth as we go. You will join a very entrepreneurial team, driven by curiosity about the technology, with a desire to make an impact while working in a fun and engaging workplace. As an early employee, you will be an important contributor to building this environment along with us.

What We Offer:

A unique opportunity to be part of standing up and operating a quantum computing company with strong backers, in modern offices located centrally in the Innovation District Copenhagen with convenient public transport and lunch service.

Comprehensive remuneration package, including benefits that support an environment where people can grow and do their best work.

This position will be based in Copenhagen, which offers a rare combination of international outlook, strong quantum and deep-tech ecosystem, and excellent quality of life, consistently ranked amongst the most liveable cities in the world.

Application and Contact:

If you wish to know more about the position, please reach out to Dr. Kasra Nowrouzi, CTO at QuNorth, at kasra@qunorth.com

Please be aware that we will be reviewing applications on an ongoing basis.

All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

We look very much forward to receiving your application.

Drivetrain Engineer – Wind Power

Goldwind Denmark is looking for a Drivetrain Engineer to contribute to the development of wind turbine drivetrain systems. You will join an international engineering environment where colleagues in Denmark and China work together to develop mechanical concepts, evaluate design solutions and support their implementation.

This opportunity suits you if you enjoy combining component design with an understanding of the complete drivetrain. In a growing company with ambitious technology goals, you can influence new concepts and help turn them into practical solutions while broadening your expertise.

The role

You will develop and evaluate drivetrain concepts, balancing reliability, weight, cost and serviceability. Working with engineering specialists and suppliers, you will translate system requirements and turbine loads into mechanical solutions.

Your responsibilities include:

• Developing concepts for main shafts, bearing arrangements, housings, supporting structures and interfaces with gearboxes and generators.

• Developing mechanical designs supported by calculations, CAD models and technical specifications.

• Assessing load paths, stiffness, alignment, tolerances and component interactions alongside FEA specialists.

• Comparing solutions to improve performance, manufacturability, assembly and maintenance.

• Supporting colleagues in China during detailed design and participating in design reviews.

• Assessing suppliers’ component capabilities, resolving technical questions and supporting design verification and testing.

• Documenting recommendations, assumptions and design risks.

Your profile

You take a systematic, practical approach to engineering, develop concepts independently and challenge assumptions constructively. You involve specialists when needed, take responsibility for your work and communicate your findings clearly.

We expect you to have:

• A degree in mechanical engineering or a related discipline.

• At least five years of relevant experience in mechanical design and development.

• Practical knowledge of one or more drivetrain components, such as shafts, bearings, housings, couplings or gearbox support arrangements.

• A solid grounding in strength, fatigue, stiffness, materials and tolerances.

• Experience with 3D CAD, engineering drawings and mechanical calculations, together with the ability to interpret simulation results and use them to guide design decisions.

• Good written and spoken English and the ability to communicate effectively across teams and cultures.

Experience with rolling or plain bearings, large cast or forged components, drivetrain dynamics, prototype testing or wind turbine certification is an advantage. You will have the opportunity to influence drivetrain concepts and help develop them into practical engineering solutions. Your work will span concept development, component design, design reviews and validation, allowing you to see how technical decisions translate into working designs.

Through close collaboration with an international engineering team and specialist suppliers, you will exchange knowledge, explore different approaches and develop both your specialist expertise and your understanding of the complete drivetrain.

_**Imagine if robust test methods and reliable test equipment helped ensure the quality of both new and existing Coloplast products. That is where you come in.

You will support the full test method and equipment lifecycle, from implementation and qualification to maintenance, transfer and continuous improvement.

If you are motivated by hands-on technical problem-solving, equipment responsibility, quality assurance and data evaluation, this role offers meaningful responsibility and broad organisational impact. You will also work closely with many internal and external stakeholders, making clear communication, coordination and strong stakeholder management an important part of your success.

_“In this role, your technical judgement and ability to create robust solutions will help ensure reliable test results and compliant laboratory processes throughout the product lifecycle,” says Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory.

_**Join a skilled and collaborative laboratory team

**At our Coloplast Mørdrup site, you will join the Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory. The team consists of laboratory technicians and test method specialists who work closely together to support ongoing production, process development, quality investigations and test method activities.

You will be part of an engaged team with a strong mix of practical laboratory experience and specialist knowledge. We value curiosity, knowledge sharing, flexibility and a continuous improvement mindset.

**Own and develop test methods and equipment

**As Test Method Specialist, you will act as a one-point contact and technical superuser for selected test methods and test equipment. A significant part of the role is practical equipment responsibility. You will work hands-on with equipment and coordinate activities to ensure it is qualified, calibrated, serviced, maintained and performing as intended. Your primary responsibilities will include:

• Acting as technical owner and one-point contact for selected test methods and related test equipment

• Planning, coordinating and performing qualification of test equipment, including relocation, capacity expansion and replacement of critical parts

• Preparing and maintaining qualification protocols, reports, procedures, test method documentation and one-point lessons when needed

• Performing hands-on troubleshooting of test equipment and methods, evaluating test results and leading root cause investigations when failures occur

• Taking practical responsibility for test equipment, including service activities, calibration follow-up, preventive maintenance and ensuring that equipment performs as intended

• Handling changes, nonconformities and CAPAs related to test methods, calibration and test equipment

• Supporting compliant storage and traceability of raw data before product release

• Planning and participating in transfers of test methods and equipment to international manufacturing sites

• Providing technical support and sparring to colleagues in the Pilot Plant, Global Operations and international manufacturing sites

• Coordinating software and computer upgrades for test equipment, assessing their impact on qualification and documentation, and managing suppliers, service visits and relevant service agreements

• Participating in internal and external audits related to test methods, equipment and documentation

• Contributing to continuous improvement of laboratory processes, systems and ways of working

You enjoy working directly with equipment, take ownership and work systematically when resolving technical issues. You are comfortable making decisions based on data, risk and regulatory requirements.

The role involves close collaboration with many internal and external stakeholders, therefor you communicate clearly, coordinate effectively and are able to build strong working relationships across functions, sites and suppliers.

We imagine that you bring:

• A master’s degree within science, engineering, mechanics, physics, chemistry, pharmacy or a comparable technical field, or have at least five years of relevant experience with test methods

• Solid hands-on experience with test methods, measurement principles and qualification of laboratory or production test equipment

• Strong problem-solving skills and experience with structured root cause analysis

• Confident evaluating, analysing and presenting technical data skills, including the use of statistical methods

• Ability to write, review and understand technical documentation, protocols and reports

• Knowledge of quality systems and regulated environments; knowledge of ISO 9001, ISO 13485 and GMP is an advantage

• An understanding of validation, calibration, design control, specifications and process risk management

• Abitlity to plan and prioritise your work effectively and follow activities through to completion

• Strong stakeholder management skills and collaborate effectively across disciplines, functions, geographical locations and external suppliers

• Communicating skills professionally in English, both written and spoken; Danish is an advantage

• A comfortable competence using digital tools for documentation, data analysis and traceability; experience with Microsoft Office, Veeva, JMP or similar systems is an advantage

**A specialist role with broad impact

**This is a permanent specialist position in the QA Lifecycle Laboratory. The role has no direct reports and includes collaboration with international colleagues and manufacturing sites. Some travel may be expected in connection with transfers, supplier activities and site support.

You will join a working environment where quality, safety, technical excellence, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement are central to our daily work. You will have the opportunity to build a broad network and influence how test methods and equipment are managed across the product lifecycle.
